project.name: Quadrotor propulsion — four independent ESC channels
project.description: Four STM32L476 six-step controllers and four reduced-order BLDC plants, with separate fault inputs and 60/64/68/72% duty commands.
project.readme:
# Four-channel propulsion bench

Each STM32L476 runs its own TIM1 six-step commutator. Rotor 1–4 use duty commands 600, 640, 680 and 720 per mille. The HALL LOCKED marker requires consecutive Hall transitions and encoder feedback. Press FAULT 1–4 to latch off the corresponding inverter. Reset that controller to rearm.

These are reduced-order motor/inverter models. This is not the physical AT32F421/AM32 4-in-1 ESC, a MOSFET transient simulation, field-oriented control or a flying aircraft. Hosted four-node verification currently depends on the generic Cortex-M world artifact-loading correction (LabWired #3094). Per-channel spin and injected-fault evidence is recorded in w1ne/labwired-examples/examples/robotics/quadrotor-bldc.
